title: Exposure Triangle in the Field
description: Set aperture, shutter and ISO for real briefs, diagnose rejected frames, and shoot a wedding as the light drops.

nodes.title: Briefing
nodes.summary: You'll work through three jobs with a camera whose dials move in full stops. Each time, you decide what the picture is about and pay for it in stops.

points.title: The meter reading
points.body: Every scene comes with one combination the camera's meter calls correctly exposed. It is a starting point, not an answer: any combination with the same total light is just as bright.

points.title: Your dials
points.body: Aperture f/1.4 to f/16, shutter 1/2000 s to 1/4 s, ISO 100 to 6400, each one stop per click.

points.title: What the photo shows you
points.body: After you shoot you see a simulated frame, with brightness, blur, shake and grain as your settings would give them, plus a short readout of what a viewer would notice.

nodes.title: Three frames, one light
nodes.mission_goal: Put the shot's priority first and trade stops so the brightness stays right

nodes.title: The reject pile
nodes.mission_goal: Trace a flaw in a photo back to the setting behind it, and fix it without creating a new one

nodes.title: Into the blue hour
nodes.mission_goal: Shoot a list of shots as the light falls, planning ahead so the hardest one isn't left to ISO
